Mina —

Thanks for the earlier topology diagram. During our tabletop last week the team flagged a concern: if a sidecar process on a node crashes repeatedly, we could see a cascading set of failures as requests are retried and KV cache invalidations spike. For our auditors we need: 

- A concise playbook that describes detection, automated mitigation, and manual escalation steps for a sidecar failure cascade.
- An annotated topology that highlights where circuit breakers, health probes, and fallback routing live.
- Short threat scenarios (2–3 bullets) showing what would happen if a sidecar fails in a hot zone + suggested mitigations.

Can you share a draft by Monday? Attachments (PDF/PNG) are fine. Also cc'ing our infra lead if they have questions.

Appreciate it —
Sam

Hi Sam —

Thanks for the clear ask. Attached are two artifacts: a one-page playbook (sidecar-failure-playbook-v1.pdf) and an annotated topology export (altum-annotated-topology.png). High-level summary below; full details are in the PDF.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Detection: sidecar liveness checks + system-level OOM/segfault counters; alert if >3 restarts within 5m for a host pool.
- Automated mitigation: isolate offending node via autoscaler cordon -> redirect new traffic to warm pool; step down concurrent inflight token acceptance through the gateway (short reject with Retry-After).
- Circuit breakers: per-route token-based backpressure plus per-host connection caps; global circuit that trips to model-variant fallback when KV cache pressure exceeds threshold.
- Cache hygiene: prefer soft eviction and background rehydration; on mass invalidation, temporarily fall back to cold-cache path for a subset of traffic to avoid thundering herd.
- Manual escalation: SOC/Platform on-call, snapshot logs and provide node ID + heapdump; escalation checklist in the playbook.

Ben and Irene — can you review the threat bullets on page 2 and the automated mitigation sequence? I'm particularly calling out the fallback ordering between (1) local retry, (2) route to warm pool, and (3) fallback to a smaller-model variant. We need to make sure this order matches our SLA and privacy constraints.

Sam — if this looks good I can turn the PDF into a one-slide flow for your auditors. Also propose a 30m walkthrough next Wednesday to step through the circuit breaker thresholds.

Mina

--
Mina Haddad
Security Architect, Redwood Inference

Mina / Sam —

Quick technical clarifications and additions after reviewing the playbook draft:

1) Failure vectors we tested (short bullets for auditor):
   - Memory leak in sidecar (long-tail growth) -> host OOM -> rapid restarts -> connection resets to model runtime.
   - Thundering KV cache invalidation (bad write storm) -> persistent cache miss amplification -> backend pressure.
   - Network partition where sidecar cannot reach control plane but continues accepting traffic -> stale routing decisions and non-idempotent retries.

2) Automated mitigation sequence (detailed order):
   - Detect: host-level restart counter OR sidecar health flapping metric.
   - Slow-path: mark node as "degraded" and reduce concurrency by 50% for new requests; enable short-circuit rejects with Retry-After header for non-critical routes.
   - Warm-pool drain: route new sessions to warm pool nodes; start graceful drain of Kafka-ish queues on the affected node to allow in-flight tokens to complete.
   - Cache triage: if KV miss rate > X% for 2m, switch 10% of traffic to no-cache path (cold read) to reduce amplification while preserving tail latency for majority.
   - Fallback escalate: if warm-pool saturation > 70% and error-rate rises, trigger model-variant fallback (smaller quantized model) for low-priority requests.

3) Observability hooks (evidence for auditors):
   - Per-node restart logs, sidecar stderr capture, aggregated KV miss heatmaps, and a k8s event snapshot file.
   - Synthetic canary traffic that exercises cache warmup; retention of the last 72h for these metrics and a portable report.

4) Security notes:
   - Fallback to smaller models preserves no additional PII; all model-variant fallbacks are logged and labeled for audit.
   - Circuit-breaker control plane uses mTLS-authenticated control channel; key rotation is covered by our KMS integration (doc link in PDF).

I made two small edits to the playbook PDF (page 3: added the exact metric thresholds we test against). Please confirm the thresholds look OK to you, Mina, and Sam.

Ben
